Read the digits a scanner drew with pipes and underscores, three columns and four rows per digit, and join several lines of them with commas.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/ocr-numbers) (MIT). Listed under [Parsing & Validation](/examples/?subject=parsing-and-validation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: ocr_numbers.nomi
//# Reads digits drawn with pipes and underscores, three columns by four rows
//# each.

/// Why rows cannot be read.
pub enum Error {
    LinesNotMultipleOfFour
    ColumnsNotMultipleOfThree
}

/// The ten digits as the scanner draws them, 0 to 9, three columns and four
/// rows each.
once font = [
    " _     _  _     _  _  _  _  _ ",
    "| |  | _| _||_||_ |_   ||_||_|",
    "|_|  ||_  _|  | _||_|  ||_| _|",
    "                              ",
]

/// Each digit's drawing, its four rows of three characters joined, to the
/// digit.
once digits = font |> glyphs() |> Iter.zip("0123456789") |> Iter.to_map()

/// The number `rows` draw: each four rows are a line of digits, each three
/// columns a digit, and the lines are joined by commas. A drawing that is
/// no digit reads as `?`.
pub fn convert(rows: List<String>) -> Result<String, Error> {
    if Iter.count(rows) % 4 != 0 {
        Err(.LinesNotMultipleOfFour)
    } else if Iter.any(rows, &(String.length(&1) % 3 != 0)) {
        Err(.ColumnsNotMultipleOfThree)
    } else {
        rows
        |> Iter.chunks(4)
        |> Iter.map(read_line)
        |> String.join(",")
        |> Ok()
    }
}

/// The digits one line of four rows draws.
fn read_line(line: List<String>) -> String {
    line
    |> glyphs()
    |> Iter.map(&(Map.get(digits, &1) |> Maybe.with_default("?")))
    |> String.join()
}

/// Each digit's drawing in four `rows`, left to right: the rows cut into
/// three-column cells, read down each column of cells.
fn glyphs(rows: List<String>) -> List<String> {
    rows
    |> Iter.map(fn row -> row |> Iter.chunks(3) |> Iter.map(String.join))
    |> Iter.transpose()
    |> Iter.map(String.join)
    |> Iter.to_list()
}

test "convert" {

            ],
            Ok("3"),
        ),
        #(
            "Recognizes 4",
            [
                "   ",
                "|_|",
                "  |",
                "   ",
            ],
            Ok("4"),
        ),
        #(
            "Recognizes 5",
            [
                " _ ",
                "|_ ",
                " _|",
                "   ",
            ],
            Ok("5"),
        ),
        #(
            "Recognizes 6",
            [
                " _ ",
                "|_ ",
                "|_|",
                "   ",
            ],
            Ok("6"),
        ),
        #(
            "Recognizes 7",
            [
                " _ ",
                "  |",
                "  |",
                "   ",
            ],
            Ok("7"),
        ),
        #(
            "Recognizes 8",
            [
                " _ ",
                "|_|",
                "|_|",
                "   ",
            ],
            Ok("8"),
        ),
        #(
            "Recognizes 9",
            [
                " _ ",
                "|_|",
                " _|",
                "   ",
            ],
            Ok("9"),
        ),
        #(
            "Recognizes string of decimal numbers",
            [
                "    _  _     _  _  _  _  _  _ ",
                "  | _| _||_||_ |_   ||_||_|| |",
                "  ||_  _|  | _||_|  ||_| _||_|",
                "                              ",
            ],
            Ok("1234567890"),
        ),
        #(
            "Numbers separated by empty lines are recognized. Lines are joined by commas.",
            [
                "    _  _ ",
                "  | _| _|",
                "  ||_  _|",
                "         ",
                "    _  _ ",
                "|_||_ |_ ",
                "  | _||_|",
                "         ",
                " _  _  _ ",
                "  ||_||_|",
                "  ||_| _|",
                "         ",

            Ok("123,456,789"),
        ),

    subtests cases, #(description, rows, expected), description {
```

## How it's written

- `convert` returns `Result<String, Error>`. The two canonical errors, a row count that is not a multiple of four and a row width that is not a multiple of three, are the `Error` variants `LinesNotMultipleOfFour` and `ColumnsNotMultipleOfThree`. A drawing that is no digit is not an error: it reads as `?`, as the canonical data asks.
- The digits are not a hand-written table of twelve-character keys. `font` is the ten digits drawn the way the input draws them, and `digits` reads the font with the same `glyphs` function the input goes through, zipped with `"0123456789"` into a map. The font and the reader cannot disagree.
- `glyphs` cuts each row into three-column cells (`Iter.chunks(3)` over the row's graphemes, each cell joined back into a `String`), then `Iter.transpose` turns four rows of cells into the cells of each digit, top to bottom, and each digit's cells are joined into one key.
- The lines are `Iter.chunks(4)` over the rows, each read with `read_line` and joined with commas. A cell drawing missing from `digits` is the `?` the canonical data expects, so `Maybe.with_default("?")` is the rule, not a guess.
- `String.join` is passed as a function, `Iter.map(String.join)`; its separator defaults to `""`.
- The 17 canonical cases are one `subtests` table. Each row's drawing is a list written one string per line, so the rows read as the picture they are.
